statement_record.book: In the category of sets and partial functions (which has a zero object): (i) give a formula for the binary coproduct A v B; (ii) give a formula for the binary product A x B; (iii) the identity matrix gives a canonical map I : A v B -> A x B, and the smash product A ^ B is the pushout of I along the unique map A v B -> 0; give a formula for A ^ B.
statement_record.intree: Part_Cartesian: '@Cartesian Part := { product_obj := fun x y => {| carrier := x + (y + (x * y)) |} }'; Par_Cocartesian: '@Cocartesian Par := { product_obj := sum; ... }'; Par_Initial/Par_Terminal both at the empty type.

evidence.intree_statement: Class DoubleCategory : Type := { dcat : Category;  dhor : dcat -> dcat -> Type;  dsq {a b c d : dcat} : dhor a b -> (a ~{dcat}~> c) -> (b ~{dcat}~> d) -> dhor c d -> Type;  dsq_setoid ...;  dsq_vid {a b} (h : dhor a b) : dsq h id id h;  dsq_vcomp ... : dsq h u v k -> dsq k u' v' l -> dsq h (u' o u) (v' o v) l;  dhid (a : dcat) : dhor a a;  dhcomp {a b c : dcat} : dhor b c -> dhor a b -> dhor a c;  dsq_hcomp ... : dsq h u v k -> dsq h' v w k' -> dsq (dhcomp h' h) u w (dhcomp k' k);  dinterchange ...;  dassoc ...; dunit_left ...; dunit_right ...; dcoherence_triangle ...; dcoherence_pentagon ... }  -- i.e. exactly the elementary unpacking the exercise asks for: objects and STRICT vertical morphisms (the objects and morphisms of dcat), horizontal 1-cells dhor, squares dsq with their four boundary edges, identities and compositions in both directions, and interchange

statement_record.book: A double category is an internal category in Cat, i.e. the diagram (3.6.12) of categories and functors dom, cod : C1 => C0, id : C0 -> C1, comp : C1 x_{C0} C1 -> C1. Unpack this into elementary data: objects and 'horizontal morphisms' (objects and morphisms of C0), 'vertical morphisms' and 'squares' (objects and morphisms of C1), with domains, codomains, identities and compositions defined both internally to C0 and C1 and by the functors in the diagram.
statement_record.intree: Class DoubleCategory : Type := { dcat : Category; dhor : dcat -> dcat -> Type; dsq {a b c d} : dhor a b -> (a ~> c) -> (b ~> d) -> dhor c d -> Type; dsq_vid; dsq_vcomp; dhid; dhcomp; dsq_hcomp; dinterchange; dassoc; dunit_left; dunit_right; dcoherence_triangle; dcoherence_pentagon }
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in the horizontal direction and different in packaging. (a) The in-tree class is a PSEUDO double category: dassoc/dunit_left/dunit_right are only INVERTIBLE GLOBULAR squares subject to triangle+pentagon, whereas an internal category in Cat is a STRICT double category with dhcomp strictly associative and unital. (b) The internal-category presentation itself (the pullback C1 x_{C0} C1 in Cat and the functors dom/cod/id/comp) is not defined in-tree at all, so the exercise's actual task -- deriving the elementary data FROM that diagram, and hence the equivalence of the two presentations -- is absent. (c) The header of Theory/DoubleCategory.v discloses a coherence-only scope: horizontal identity squares on verticals, unit-interchange, and coherence naturality are not required by the class. (d) Naming is transposed relative to Riehl: in-tree the morphisms of dcat are the VERTICAL 1-cells while dhor carries the horizontal ones.

gap: The internal-category-in-Cat definition (diagram 3.6.12) and the unpacking correspondence are missing. grep -rn -i -E 'internal categ|InternalCat|category object|pullback of categories|C_1' over *.v returns only prose: Theory/DoubleCategory.v:115-116 ('a double category is precisely a category internal to Cat') and Construction/Enriched.v:83-85 (contrasting enrichment with internal categories).
